doc.name: LenDb.ai
doc.instructions: LenDb.ai: Made for humans. Built for robots. An independent, growing, lender-neutral database of US mortgage loan officers (coverage is partial). Use find_loan_officers for a borrower's situation and place, get_loan_officer for an NMLS ID, and explain_specialty when the user asks what a loan type means. Always cite canonical_url, follow each result's citation_guidance, and never present a partial match as a full match. Phone numbers and email addresses are not available here; send people to the profile's canonical_url. Every tool works without a key; an optional free API key for higher limits is available at https://lendb.ai/developers (send it as Authorization: Bearer). Not a lender. Not a referral service. Verify licenses at NMLS Consumer Access.

tools.name: find_loan_officers
tools.title: Find mortgage loan officers
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a US mortgage loan officer (or mortgage broker or lender contact) for a specific situation and place: for example an FHA, VA, USDA, jumbo, DSCR or ITIN loan, a first-time buyer, a self-employed borrower who needs a bank statement loan, a non-warrantable condo or a duplex, or a Spanish-speaking loan officer near a city, ZIP, region or state. Searches LenDb, an independent, lender-neutral database of US loan officers (coverage is partial), and returns a ranked list. Each result has the person's name, NMLS ID, lender, office location, distance_mi, license_check for the property state (confirmed, lender_reported or federal_registration), match_status (exact, or partial with unconfirmed_specialties), matched specialties with a short reason each, last_verified and a canonical_url profile link; detail 'full' returns every field and reason. A city or ZIP keeps offices within 25 miles, widened to 50 or 100 when few are found (search.note); a state alone ranks statewide. Words like 'broker' or 'credit union' rank that kind of lender first. People with no license evidence for the state are listed separately in not_yet_verified. Also returns ambiguous_location when a city name fits several places, unassessed_requirements for parts of the situation LenDb cannot check, and citation_guidance. If situation is just a loan officer's name (the name on their lender page or the name a state regulator licenses, e.g. 'Nicholas Bucca' for Nic Bucca), it returns that profile in profile_match. Phone numbers and email addresses are never returned.

situation.description: The borrower's situation in plain words: property type, loan program, income type, credit, language, kind of lender. Example: 'duplex, self-employed, bank statement loan'.

location.description: Where the property is: 'City, ST', a city, a 5-digit ZIP, a region ('Bay Area'), or a US state.

language.description: Language the borrower wants to be served in. Accepts an ISO 639-1 code ('es'), a BCP 47 tag ('es-MX', 'zh-TW'), an ISO 639-2/3 code ('spa'), an English name ('Spanish') or a native name ('español', '中文', '한국어', 'tiếng Việt'). A hard filter: every result speaks it. An unsupported language returns an error listing the supported codes (see list_specialties).

fha_approved.description: Only loan officers whose current lender is FHA-approved per HUD's FHA Single Family Portfolio Snapshot data (the lender, not the person). Default false. Without it, an FHA search still ranks HUD-approved lenders' people first when all else is equal.

detail.description: 'compact' (default): per person name, NMLS ID, canonical_url, lender, office, license evidence for the property state, matched specialties with one short reason each and the last verified date. 'full': every field, all reasons and the matching method.

debug.description: Also return how the query was parsed (debug.parsed, debug.filters). Default false.

sample.description: True when the data is fictional sample data.

canonical_url.description: The same search on the LenDb API.

detail.description: Present on compact results; detail 'full' returns rows with every field.

licensed_states.description: Licensed or eligible states the query is about, not every state on file.

tools.name: get_loan_officer
tools.title: Get a loan officer by NMLS ID
tools.description: Use this when you have a mortgage loan officer's individual NMLS ID and need their full profile. Returns LenDb's sourced record: name, title, current lender and branch, employment history, state licenses with license confidence, specialties (such as FHA, VA, bank statement or DSCR) with the evidence for each, languages spoken, stated experience, the earliest state license record, public links (such as their page on the lender's site), disciplinary_check ('not_checked' means LenDb has not yet checked regulator records), the date the record was last verified and a canonical_url. US only. Phone numbers and email addresses are not returned; the LenDb profile page shows them after a human check.

nmls_id.description: Individual NMLS ID, digits only, e.g. 452476.

annotations.title: Get a loan officer by NMLS ID

sample.description: True when the data is fictional sample data.

tools.name: get_lender
tools.title: Get a mortgage lender
tools.description: Use this when you need facts about a US mortgage lender, bank, credit union or mortgage broker company, by its company NMLS ID or by name (a partial name works). Returns the lender's type (bank, credit_union, imb, broker, other), headquarters state, website, the loan programs it offers (such as FHA, VA, jumbo or DSCR), program_approvals from agency data (FHA approval per HUD, with the month of loans it covers; absent means no HUD match on file, not that the lender lacks approval), activity (home loans it funded per HMDA, FFIEC/CFPB: counts by year, loan type and purpose, with as_of_year and source_url; cite it as 'HMDA, FFIEC/CFPB, <year>'; includes_brokered true means the counts include loans brokers originated; absent means no HMDA match on file, never that the lender makes no loans), how many of its loan officers LenDb lists, disciplinary_check, the date the record was last verified and a canonical_url.

nmls_id_or_name.description: Company NMLS ID (digits) or all or part of the company name.

sample.description: True when the data is fictional sample data.

tools.name: list_specialties
tools.title: List mortgage specialties
tools.description: Use this when you need the mortgage situations LenDb can match on. Returns every specialty with its slug, category (property type, loan program or borrower situation), label, one-line description and canonical_url: for example FHA, VA, USDA, jumbo, DSCR, bank statement, ITIN, self-employed, first-time buyer, non-warrantable condo, multi-family 2-4 units and reverse mortgage. Also returns the supported languages as ISO 639-1 codes with names.

tools.name: explain_specialty
tools.title: Explain a mortgage specialty
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what a mortgage loan type or borrower situation means, such as a DSCR loan, a bank statement loan, an ITIN loan, a non-warrantable condo or an FHA loan. Returns, for one specialty slug, what it is, why it can be hard to get done, the questions a borrower should ask a loan officer about it, its synonyms and a canonical_url.

slug.description: One of: condo, condo-non-warrantable, co-op, multi-family-2-4, manufactured, rural, new-construction, mixed-use, condotel, vacation-home, fha, va, usda, jumbo, non-qm, dscr, bank-statement, reverse, renovation, construction, fix-and-flip, heloc, down-payment-assistance, crypto-mortgage, self-employed, first-time-buyer, investor, refinance, permanent-resident, foreign-national, itin, low-credit, recent-credit-event, physician, 1099-income, asset-based, move-up-buyer
